headline: Goldman Sachs Cuts Brazilian Stocks to Neutral as Selic Rate Stays High
summary: Goldman Sachs downgraded Brazilian equities to neutral, noting limited room for rate cuts while the central bank maintains the Selic rate at 13.75%.
why: Brazil's benchmark Selic interest rate profoundly influences domestic asset valuations, borrowing costs, and foreign equity inflows into Latin America's largest economy.

impacts.name: Brazil Bovespa Index
impacts.why: A broker downgrade combined with a high key interest rate dampens equity valuation multiples and investor allocations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Persistent high interest rates restrict monetary easing scope, prompting institutional brokers to lower regional equity recommendations.
